newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli privatisation plan lacks details.
newsitem.headline: Israeli privatisation plan lacks details.

text.p: The privatisation plan due to be unveiled by the Israeli government contains a list of companies to be sold but no programme for implementation, a senior official in the prime minister's office said on Sunday.

Moshe Leon, deputy director-general in the prime minister's office in charge of economic affairs, told Reuters the list of companies to be sold off by the government next year included Bezeq Israel Telecom, Israel Chemicals Ltd and property companies he refused to identify.
But he said the plan did not address when the sales would occur, how they would be done or what portion of the companies would be sold.

Leon said the plan also called for selling major holdings in the commercial banks. He refused to say which banks or to comment on newspaper reports that the government planned to publish a tender for a controlling stake in Bank Leumi in response to renewed interest from foreign investors.

Leon said the government's strategy was to pursue privatisation by selling holdings in state enterprises and reforming industrial sectors at a rate of two per year. In 1997, the focus would be on telecommunications and public transport, he added.
This month, a government committee proposed opening up the last remaining segments of the telecommunications market to competition by the end of 1998.
Leon said "I hope very much" that the privatisation programme would be unveiled next week.
